key_insight: PISA (Preconditioned Inexact Stochastic ADMM) is an optimizer that lets deep models be trained with heterogeneous data and a wide range of preconditioners, providing provable convergence under weak assumptions while empirically outperforming popular optimizers.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between practical optimizer flexibility (heterogeneous data, custom preconditioners, approximate subproblem solves) and rigorous convergence guarantees for nonconvex deep learning models.
method: Formulate training as a stochastic ADMM scheme with preconditioning to decouple model subproblems and accommodate heterogeneous data sources.
Allow inexact (approximate) inner solves and stochastic updates to keep computation scalable, while carefully controlling errors to preserve convergence.
Provide unified theory proving convergence under minimal assumptions and demonstrate empirical gains across diverse tasks and preconditioners.
impact: Offers practitioners a flexible, scalable optimizer that supports custom preconditioning and heterogeneous/distributed data with theoretical guarantees—leading to more reliable training and better empirical performance.
visual_elements: Algorithm flowchart: ADMM split showing primal/dual updates, preconditioner blocks, and inexact inner solvers.
Benchmark chart: convergence curves (loss vs. iterations) comparing PISA to Adam/SGD across several tasks/datasets.
System diagram: heterogeneous data sources or clients feeding into a central model with different preconditioners (illustrates federated/distributed use).
Summary panel: compact table of assumptions vs. guarantees (what is required and what is proved).
paper_title: Preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM for deep models
paper_authors: Shenglong Zhou, Ouya Wang, Ziyan Luo, Yongxu Zhu, Geoffrey Ye Li
